answer: In a decentralized consensus network, a Sybil-resistant mechanism is reputation-based proof-of-stake, where validators' identities are tied to unique, costly-to-create cryptographic anchors. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to expend resources comparable to constructing a secure jetty on a karst coastline, only to see their reputation plummet to its nadir as their false identities are detected and penalized, thereby securing the network at a fraction of the cost of a successful attack.
